title: Manage accepted changes and ticket references
purpose: Track implementation separately from suggestion alignment and SOP publication approval.

content.scope: Process owners, implementation owners, and suggestion participants

steps.what: Accept a suggestion. A planned change record is created automatically. The accepted suggestion displays an implementation summary and a Manage implementation link. N/A means no underlying concern applies; Undetermined means assessment is still needed.
steps.notes: Existing accepted suggestions also receive a planned change record.

steps.what: Open the linked change, confirm the implementation owner, and record the plan and planned dates. Additional accepted suggestions for the same process can be linked. Only the process owner can reassign implementation ownership.
steps.notes: Linked SOP revisions appear through their accepted suggestions.

steps.what: Add a ticket reference using its system name, ticket number, and full HTTP or HTTPS URL. Save with a progress update or reason. The saved ticket number opens the external ticket. These references are manually entered; no external ticket is created or synchronized automatically.

Move through Planned, In progress, Ready for validation, Implemented, and Effectiveness verified as work completes. Record evidence for implementation and verification. Use Blocked or Cancelled with an explanation when appropriate. Resume blocked or cancelled work at an implementation stage before validation.
steps.notes: This status never approves an SOP publication or closes a linked suggestion or defect.

steps.what: Use the collapsed Activity log or Communication log at the bottom of a workflow when reviewing history. Expand it to read the smaller, scrollable entries. Return to the suggestion to document outcome verification and explicit submitter agreement.
steps.notes: History remains retained even though logs are collapsed during normal use.

title: Suggest a change and reach verified alignment
purpose: Raise an improvement, receive a documented response, and resolve the underlying concern through agreement and evidence.

content.scope: Suggestion submitters, process owners, managers, and administrators

steps.what: Open Suggestions & alignment and choose Suggest a change. Drill through the organization hierarchy to the specific process. Optionally select a related published SOP. Enter a title, current problem or opportunity, proposed change, and expected benefit. Cost and ROI estimates are optional; include currency, timeframe, and assumptions when useful.
steps.notes: You can also use Suggest a change from an open SOP to preselect its process and document.

steps.what: Open the submitted suggestion. Assess the underlying concern and explain the decision to the submitter. Accept for implementation, request clarification, or decline the proposed solution with a selected decline reason. Declining a solution does not close the concern.
steps.notes: Acceptance is separate from SOP publication approval.

steps.what: Read the response. Provide requested clarification, agree with the explanation and next steps, or challenge it with an explanation. A challenge remains Alignment unresolved and is visible to the owner, their manager, and administrators for follow-up.
steps.notes: Opening a notification does not count as acknowledgment or agreement.

steps.what: Record a corrective action or training plan and effectiveness review date. Keep temporary containment explicitly marked. Document training and understanding evidence, defect correction evidence, or both as appropriate. After the effectiveness review, propose the verified resolution for the submitter's agreement.
steps.notes: Unresolved defects have a separate queue and remain visible even when the proposed solution was declined.

steps.what: Review the resolution and evidence. Explicitly agree to close the concern, or challenge it if the issue remains. Reopen a closed concern if it recurs. Communication history retains decisions, messages, participants, timestamps, and in-app availability.
steps.notes: In-app availability is not proof that someone read or agreed to a message. Email delivery is not enabled in this preview.

steps.what: Open a published client SOP in SOP Workspace and choose Start revision. Select an accepted suggestion and enter the change rationale. The relevant process owner may start directly with a rationale. Admins and managers need an accepted suggestion when they are not the process owner. Submit the draft through the existing publication approval workflow.
steps.notes: Publishing the revision does not close the suggestion. New SOP creation remains available without a suggestion.

title: Create and submit your first SOP
purpose: Practice the authoring workflow using a private draft and a controlled submission.

steps.what: Open New SOP in the SOP workspace. Choose the organization group, department, subdepartment, process family, and process the procedure describes. In the local practice environment, use Practice workflows.

Enter a clear title, a purpose describing the expected outcome, and procedure steps using Who, What, and Where. Use Add step as needed, and move steps to set their order. Gatekeeper numbers and formats them consistently. Select Create draft. Only you can edit this draft.
Make any additional changes and select Save copy. The saved draft is not published. You can return to it from My work & reviews.
Complete the title, purpose, and Who, What, and Where for every step and select Submit for approval. Submission freezes a candidate, records your participation, and assigns eligible approvers.

Follow the request's Activity and your Notifications. The published library changes only after approval. If your submission is rejected, use Revise rejected submission to create a linked new attempt when the published base has not changed.
Practice exercise: sign in as demo.author and submit a procedure for checking a workstation before starting a shift. Sign out, then sign in as demo.owner to review it.

title: Review a candidate and propose edits
purpose: Use process expertise to review a submitted SOP without overwriting the author's snapshot.

steps.what: Open My work & reviews and select an assigned request. Read the submitted candidate and compare it with the published version when one exists.
If the candidate is ready, select Approve & publish. If it needs to return to the author, enter a reason and select Reject with reason.
To make the correction yourself, select Edit a private copy. Make changes and select Save copy. Other participants still see the submitted candidate, not your private edits.

Enter the change reason, then select Submit revised candidate. The earlier candidate remains in version comparison. The new candidate becomes the one awaiting approval, and routing is recalculated using all recorded participants.

After contributing, do not expect an ordinary approval action for your own work. When you are the relevant process owner, your manager or an eligible administrator can independently approve the revised candidate.
Practice exercise: as demo.owner, edit a candidate submitted by demo.author. Submit the revised candidate, then sign in as demo.manager and approve it.

title: Record an accountable self-approval
purpose: Understand the restricted self-approval exception and its audit trail.

steps.what: Open a submitted request to which you contributed. Self-approval is offered only when you are the relevant process owner or an administrator and current routing permits it.
Prefer independent review when appropriate. For a process owner's submission, the manager or an eligible administrator can approve. A manager's submission is reviewed by the process owner.
When exercising the self-approval exception, enter a specific reason explaining why you are approving your own contribution. A blank reason is not accepted.

Select Self-approve & publish. The decision records your identity, contribution, and reason. The designated approvers, manager, and administrators receive the applicable notifications, with duplicate recipients removed.
Review Activity and Notifications. This local preview stores email notifications in the outbox but does not send email or provide a delivery report yet.
Practice exercise: create and submit a separate SOP as demo.owner. Verify that self-approval is unavailable until you enter a reason.

title: Revise a published SOP and compare versions
purpose: Keep the current publication stable while reviewing proposed changes and earlier versions.

steps.what: Select a client SOP in Published SOPs. Gatekeeper guides are maintained by the product and cannot be edited through client revision workflows.

Select Start revision. If the SOP uses an earlier format, select Use standard template. Review the original text copied into the first What field, split it into steps, and complete Who and Where. Edit and save your private copy, then submit it for approval. The current publication stays visible throughout review.
In the request, compare the candidate with the current publication. Use Compare from and Compare to to inspect any submitted candidate in this request.

After approval, reopen the SOP in Published SOPs. Its version selectors include its published history, with the latest publication selected by default. Comparison dropdowns show hierarchy codes, process family, process, SOP title, and publication version (v1, v2, and so on). Unpublished submissions use Candidate labels, with the current candidate identified.

If another publication or routing change makes your screen stale, preserve any unsaved text and reload the request. The application blocks a stale save or decision instead of silently overwriting newer work.

Structured versions use the same layout side by side with added, edited, and moved step indicators. Earlier publications retain their original format. Word-level highlighting, document intake, and historical imports will be added in later releases.

title: Set up organization and approval ownership
purpose: Connect the organization hierarchy to SOP authoring and accountable approval routing.

steps.what: Sign in as an administrator and open Admin. Create the organization, organization groups, departments, subdepartments, process families, and business processes in that order. Create user accounts for process owners and reviewers.
Open Admin > Workflow setup. Select the deployment organization if it has not been configured. The client organization cannot be changed here after setup.

Select a process, assign its owner account, and choose the direct manager. A manager is optional when an administrator will provide independent approval. A reporting line applies to every process owned by that person.
Enter a reason and save the ownership assignment. Review the configuration activity record. If a concurrent change is reported, refresh and check the current values.

Sign in as an author and select New SOP. Confirm that the process appears under its group, department, and family. If ownership changes during review, an administrator must recalculate approvers before a decision.

When creating or editing hierarchy entries, select each parent in order. Each dropdown contains only children of the preceding selection. Changing a parent clears the selections beneath it. A process inherits its subdepartment through its required process family.

Review any General (migration review) subdepartments. Open Business Process Families, edit the affected family, and select the correct subdepartment within its current department. Existing published snapshots retain their original contents.

Find a hierarchy entry by selecting each parent in order. Options display code and name, sorted numerically by code; entries marked Needs code appear last alphabetically. Stop at the level you want to update, confirm the full path, enter its code and a reason, and save. Changing a parent clears all lower selections.

Open SOP Library in the top navigation. This page lists published SOPs; drafts and review candidates remain in SOP Workspace. In the workspace Published SOPs tab, use the hierarchy dropdowns to filter publications at any level. Tiles show the standard hierarchy, title, and version format, ordered by hierarchy code numbers. The tile area scrolls after four rows; use Clear filters to show all publications again.

Select your organization, then drill into groups, departments, subdepartments, process families, and processes. Every family has one required subdepartment parent. Selecting any parent shows all published SOPs beneath it. Use the path buttons to move back up.
Search within the selected branch by title, purpose, hierarchy name, or code. Read the full hierarchy path below each result. The v number counts published versions, not review candidates.
Open a result and read the current publication. Follow its purpose and ordered Who, What, and Where steps when executing the procedure.
Use History & comparison when you need earlier publications. Historical versions are reference material; use the current publication to perform the procedure.

content.scope: All users who read and perform procedures

title: Find and use a published SOP
purpose: Locate the correct procedure through the organization hierarchy and use its current approved version.
